My strategy is to hold cash to survive one hotel hit and block monopolies. Selling Park Place would create a third killer.

A dark blue hotel could bankrupt me in one hit for $1,500 to $2,000. That makes the dark blue set dangerous even if I acquire it. Building three houses on orange would cost $900 and leave a thin margin against p4 and p3's existing hotels. I am now weighing three specific counter-offer options: demanding New York Avenue plus maximum cash, simply rejecting the trade, or asking for something else.

I am now weighing whether p2 would accept New York Avenue plus cash for Park Place. They just spent $360 on Boardwalk specifically to complete the dark blue set, and New York is their orange blocker against me. A smart player might refuse because dark blue is more threatening than orange, but they could be desperate after that large purchase. The trade would give me the statistically best monopoly, though I would need cash to build immediately.

The counter-offer is now fixed at Park Place for New York Avenue plus $250 cash. p2 would retain only $34 after paying, but they could mortgage roughly $700 in other properties to build the dark blue set. I would receive about $905 total, which covers three houses on the orange group at $900 and leaves a $5 cushion. This tight margin makes the trade risky.

I am now calculating the exact financial impact of selling Park Place. Two houses on the orange group would cost $600 and leave me with only $305 in cash. The total liquid assets would drop to roughly $700, which is survivable once but not twice.

Two houses on the orange group would still leave me fragile. Three houses would cost $900 and leave only $5 cash, so I would be dead to any hotel hit even if I mortgaged Water Works. The swap is therefore too risky.

Rejecting the trade is now looking better. p2 wasted $360 on a $50 rent property, which weakens them significantly. Their cash is only $284, so they may go bankrupt to p4's hotels before I can collect.

I am now wondering what happens to p2's properties if they declare bankruptcy.

I now see a critical reason to keep Park Place. If p2 declares bankruptcy, the player who collects the debt receives their properties. If p2 goes bankrupt to me, I would gain Boardwalk and could complete the dark blue set myself. This makes holding onto Park Place far more valuable than trading it away.

p2 and p3 are both vulnerable to hotel hits, but p4 is the strongest player with $961 cash and hotels while sitting in jail. The plan is to avoid creating new monopolies for others, survive until someone declares bankruptcy, and acquire Boardwalk or Virginia if possible. The $230 offer is insulting for a monopoly completer, so I will reject it outright. A counter-offer that does not give p2 the dark blue set is impossible because they only want Park Place.

I will reject the trade outright rather than waste my single tool call on an absurd counter-offer. I may privately note that p2 now owns Boardwalk, confirming Park Place must never be sold to them.

The inheritance risk from p2 now depends on a direct sale, since p3 no longer owns Boardwalk. I am also mapping the current color ownership: p2 holds Indiana and North Carolina, p3 holds Pacific, and p4 holds Ventnor and Pennsylvania. Marvin Gardens is yellow, and Atlantic is unowned.

I will reject the trade outright. I am drafting a firm public message that mocks p2 for wasting $360 on Boardwalk, and I am considering a brief deception to keep them from making other deals.
